description: A growing directory of self-contained use-case scripts (mix_install_examples style: one .exs per use case, runnable with 'elixir examples/<name>.exs'). Each example implements a real use case in pure Elixir and with defk, checks they agree, measures both, and prints a machine-readable DEFK_RESULT line with a verdict. examples/run_all.exs aggregates them into a scoreboard. The catalog must include poor fits too, so the docs can say clearly what defk is good at and what not to use it for.

comments.text: Ordering rule for new catalog entries (owner, 2026-10-09): we do not exclude a job on principle because the BEAM or a library already does it; every plausible job gets an entry with a pre-registered expected verdict, so the catalog guides people. Priority goes to what defk can make better: expected-good entries with a real anchor first (P2), guidance entries where Elixir or a BIF is expected to win second (P3-P4). The text workloads from docs/research/string-workloads.md (defk-dtw.20) and the Monte Carlo and hash-chain jobs are filed under this rule below.

Sibling epics filed 2026-10-09: defk-52v (from-scratch kernels where people wrap a library; Tier 1 and 2 entries are catalog examples too, parented there to keep the rewrite question in one place) and defk-sve (kernel-owned state: exploration then decision). The rewrite boundary table lives in defk-52v.14.

title: Example catalog: where defk is (and is not) the right tool
